source.title: Distillation ≈ Early Stopping? Harvesting Dark Knowledge Utilizing Anisotropic Information Retrieval For Overparameterized Neural Network
source.authors: Bin Dong; Jikai Hou; Yiping Lu; Zhi-Hua Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The supplied extract ends after Appendix B; no missing portion is indicated.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies overparameterized networks fitting corrupted labels and argues that they learn informative components before noise, but its experiments concern self-distillation and label refinement rather than random labels on the original setups. It explicitly attributes clean-before-wrong-label behavior to prior work, not a new test of that behavior.
record.gate_note: Relevant evidence is limited to an early-stopping distillation experiment, a noisy-label self-distillation experiment, and measurements of label-vector information in top NTK eigenspaces. Statements about fitting arbitrary labels and learning clean labels before wrong labels are attributed to cited prior work. No experiment tests random relabeling, shuffled or Gaussian inputs, explicit regularization on random labels, or whether clean and random labels are learned differently without inducing self-distillation.
record.test_reason: The study uses random-label memorization and clean-before-noisy learning to motivate distillation. Its own results concern distillation performance, label refinement and NTK spectral projections. It does not measure random-label fitting, perfect training fit across noise levels, or the temporal order of learning clean and corrupted labels. Figure 4 reports ordinary-training overfitting at one noise rate, which does not establish those effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors interpret informative information as leading NTK eigenspace components, argue that early stopping supplies dark knowledge, and propose self-distillation that can improve noisy-label learning beyond early stopping. Their clean-label recovery theorem applies to the specified two-layer network and clusterable-data assumptions; it is not a theorem about ordinary networks fitting random labels.
record.recipe_differences: This paper's principal experiments use distillation/self-distillation and noisy-label refinement, not the original random-label intervention or its measurements. It cites both original sources but does not reproduce their random-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The best student result depends on teacher training epoch: the 80-epoch teacher produces the best student. For noisy-label experiments, the self-distillation interpolation setting varies with noise rate and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: An intermediate teacher checkpoint produces the best distilled student.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher training duration affects the usefulness of its outputs for distillation.

fits_no_version.finding: Label corruption reduces top-five NTK-eigenspace projection, and self-distillation supervision usually increases that projection relative to noisy labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy labels and refined supervision differ in their alignment with leading NTK eigenspaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-distillation reports useful test accuracy under symmetric label corruption and avoids the ordinary-training overfitting described at 40% noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive self-distillation can mitigate label-noise overfitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 proves convergence to unobserved clean labels for self-distillation under clusterability, within-cluster corruption below one half, sufficient width and prescribed supervision schedules.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A specially designed self-distillation procedure can recover clean labels under restrictive structural assumptions.

record.problems: No random-label experiment; training fit is not reported for the noisy-label sweep. Key accuracy table is flattened in the supplied text, making some cell assignments ambiguous. Several relevant plots provide no numerical values. Empirical test accuracies are averages of 3 runs, but no variability estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out due to the 60-row limit. Table 1 contains comparator methods, but those rows were omitted because the study's new methods compared with other methods are not results for the claim's object; table flattening also makes full row-to-cell assignments unclear.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error and chance test performance on completely random labels under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout a corruption sweep together with steadily worsening test error toward chance. The reported sweep evaluates a label-refinement intervention without establishing training fit.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.

Direct clean-versus-noisy learning trajectories under ordinary training. The NTK argument establishes different rates for eigenspace components, but does not independently establish their correspondence to real and random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text suffices for this assessment. Unreadable figure values and uncertain table assignments are not evidence that a claim fails. Comparator omissions were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training experiment or chance test error is reported.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or convergence rate across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.

Experiments use symmetric noise rates only at p=0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8; they do not test p=1 or establish perfect training fit throughout the sweep. Results report average final test accuracy, not a steadily rising error trajectory.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
The paper cites prior clean-before-noisy memorization findings but does not itself test the temporal order of learning real versus random labels without self-distillation inducement.
